sections.headline: Agents that run your paid engine and *make the next move*.
sections.subhead: You run one of the most sophisticated CI/CD paid programs we've seen — 91 Google creatives capturing category and competitor intent, and 193 LinkedIn creatives running demand-gen, replatform conquesting and founder storytelling. card.title: 'AI Development Pipeline' is your fastest-growing angle — but shares one page with generic 'CI/CD'
card.found: Your newest, highest-intent message ('validate AI-generated code at AI speed') runs on the same destination as broad category terms — AI-native teams and generic CI/CD searchers land in the same place.
card.why: So the angle that's actually working can't be told apart from the one that isn't, and you're scaling spend blind to which message produces paying teams.
card.move: Split the AI-validation angle onto its own page and campaign, measure trial→paid separately, and shift budget from the flat generic terms toward it.
card.impact: See which angle actually produces paying teams

sections.heading: We studied how CircleCI runs paid *before writing a word*.
sections.body: Pulled from your public Google and LinkedIn ad libraries, July 2026. It's one of the most sophisticated CI/CD paid programs we've seen — two heavy channels running distinct jobs. Here's what we saw — and where an agent layer earns its keep.

channels.label: Category + competitor intent capture
channels.body: 'AI Development Pipeline,' 'Migrate to CircleCI,' vs-Bitrise comparison pages, enterprise scale + compliance — text-dominant, always-on, multi-market (incl. Japan). Bottom-of-funnel: you buy the intent.

channels.label: Demand-gen · thought leadership · replatform conquesting
channels.body: 'More than a CI/CD tool — a complete developer platform,' 'pragmatic engineers know fast feedback loops,' 'outgrown your CI/CD platform? Time to replatform,' 'works at 10 devs, breaks at 100 or 1000,' founder storytelling and AI-validation. Image- and video-heavy — your brand and switching engine.

sections.footer: Two heavy channels, 284 live creatives, and a sharp anti-incumbent switching motion. The gap isn't the ads — it's which of them actually becomes a paying team, correlated across Google intent and every LinkedIn touch and acted on daily. That's the layer Northstar Analytics owns.

sections.eyebrow: The feedback loop you don't have
sections.heading: You gave engineering fast, automated feedback on every build. Who gives your growth team that on every ad dollar?
sections.body: CircleCI exists so teams learn what broke in seconds, not in production. But your own growth engine runs the way most do — spend across Google and LinkedIn, signups in the product, revenue in the CRM — and nothing joins them daily. Northstar Analytics is that feedback loop for your ad spend: CI/CD for the paid engine — catch what's failing early, and fix it before the budget's gone.

sections.heading: Point the agents at a goal. Agents run the rest.
sections.body: Set a goal in your own terms — cost-per-paying-team on Google, enterprise pipeline by market — and the agent works out what to watch and what to do, on your numbers.

goals.text: Prove out the AI-validation angle 25% faster — without dropping signup volume.
goals.result: Agents isolate the AI-pipeline campaigns, measure trial→paid on their own, and move budget toward what converts.

goals.text: Route every enterprise-intent signup before it stalls in the compliance eval.
goals.result: Agents learn the path your enterprise wins took, catch the ones that stall on self-hosted/SOC 2, and hand them to sales.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.body: Track every Google campaign, keyword and product signup daily — against your goal and your own baseline, not a canned benchmark.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Every number is checked against source data before it reaches you — grounded analysis, not a guess.

steps.title: Recommend
steps.body: When a sustained pattern bears on the goal, surface the move in Slack: evidence, cause, action, and what it's worth.

steps.title: Act
steps.body: Approve and the agent acts — shifting budget, adding negatives, routing the account. Nothing fires until you say so.

steps.title: Learn
steps.body: Every call you make is graded into memory, so next month's recommendation fits your motion better than this one.

sections.heading: Always know your next move.
sections.body: One engine watches paid-media efficiency; the other watches signups against your golden path. Two live examples, built for CircleCI.

cards.title: 'Migrate to CircleCI' and vs-Bitrise terms convert to paid at 2.3× — but get 6% of the budget
cards.found: Migration and comparison terms pull in switchers who convert to paid teams at 2.3× your generic 'CI/CD' terms, yet the broad category creatives still absorb most of the spend.
cards.why: Those generic terms haven't lifted paid conversion in 90 days — so a large share of budget is buying volume that never becomes paying teams.
cards.move: Shift 20% of generic-category budget to the migration/comparison terms, point them at the vs-pages, and add the zero-paid long-tail terms as negatives.

cards.title: 17 enterprise-shaped teams engaged your LinkedIn 'replatform' ads, signed up, then stalled at compliance
cards.found: Over 14 days, 17 teams matching your best enterprise-win profile engaged your LinkedIn replatform/switching content, signed up from search, reached the self-hosted runner / SOC 2 evaluation, and went quiet.
cards.why: This is the exact engagement pattern before 4 of your last 6 enterprise closes — high-value teams stalling right at the compliance step, unrouted to either team.
cards.move: Route the largest teams to sales today as a named list, and enroll the rest in an activation sequence keyed to the compliance step they stalled on.
